answer:
`rustdoc`’s `auto_cfg` behavior hides certain cfg predicates by default. The current rustdoc source initializes the hidden set with:

- `test`
- `doc`
- `doctest`

[source](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/2972b5e5/src/librustdoc/clean/cfg.rs)

To hide additional predicates, apply `auto_cfg(hide(...))` at the crate root or on an item:

```rust
#![doc(auto_cfg(hide(unix)))]
```

This hides `unix` from automatically generated cfg documentation for the crate’s items and descendants. Multiple predicates, including key/value predicates, can be specified:

```rust
#![doc(auto_cfg(hide(unix, feature = "something")))]
```

`auto_cfg(hide(...))` affects automatically generated cfg markers only; it does not hide explicitly written `#[doc(cfg(...))]` attributes. It also enables `auto_cfg` at that location if it had been disabled. [RFC 3631](https://rust-lang.github.io/rfcs/3631-rustdoc-cfgs-handling.html)
